title: Subprocess-Constrained Markov Decision Processes
claim: An efficiently computable polytope approximation of an exact set stays within a small neighborhood of it, so approximation error is bounded.

abstract: Constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) typically bound expected cumulative cost from an initial state. Such a guarantee can be insufficient when a policy must remain feasible after every history it may encounter. We introduce \emph{subprocess-constrained MDPs} (S-CMDPs), which require the expected discounted cost of each continuation, conditional on any reachable history, to satisfy a bound determined by the current state. This stronger requirement changes the structure and complexity of the problem: we show that stationary policies can be strictly suboptimal, and finding even an approximately optimal stationary policy is NP-hard. We adapt a recently introduced value-set iteration framework to show that history-dependent policies surprisingly overcome both obstacles. Our polynomial-time algorithm represents such a policy implicitly: its expected reward is within $Îµ$ of the optimal feasible value, it violates each subprocess cost bound by at most $Î´$, and its action distribution can be computed in polynomial time for any given history.
